title: Design spec
description: Intended design values for a page, extracted from a design source before build and diffed against the built page afterwards. Normative definition: references/design-spec.md. Consumers must ignore unknown keys so producers and consumers can adopt fields independently.

source.description: Provenance only. No consumer fetches this; it exists so a value can be traced back to the node it came from.

frames.description: Breakpoint name → node id in the design source.

frameWidth.description: Width of the design frame these values were read at. A consumer compares at this width; at any other, positions are scaled and that must be stated, because a scaled comparison is weaker evidence.

tolerance.description: Per-category noise floors in px. Raise a noisy category rather than deleting its check.

container.description: The intended content gutter — the highest-value single entry in the file.

note.description: How the value was decided. Future readers need this more than the number.

containerSelector.description: Optional override for how a consumer finds section containers.

anchorText.description: A distinctive line of copy inside the section. Anchoring on text rather than order means adding a section does not shift every later comparison.

reuse.description: Reuse fails differently from building: an existing component dropped into a new context inherits geometry correctly and still breaks, because copy length, background or container width differ. 'reused' is a prompt to record what is different here.

differences.description: For a reused/adapted section: what differs in THIS context (longer copy, different fill, narrower container, different breakpoint behaviour).

text.description: Per text node, matched on rendered words rather than selector — class names mean nothing across the design/build boundary.

scope.description: Page chrome is excluded by default: a mega-menu repeats site copy as shorter link labels, which resolves a heading to a nav link and reports the real heading as too small. Set this to opt an entry back in.

groups.description: Named sets that look alike and differ in the design. Naming both forces the difference to exist — modelling two variants as one thing is how a variant silently gets built once.

states.description: Every dynamically-bound field and what the layout does at each extreme. Templates are built against no content and empty is the normal case, so the empty state is a design state, not an edge case.

behaviors.description: Interactive or animated behavior agreed before build. Record outcomes, not library-specific implementation details.

decisions.description: Every place the design and the existing system disagree, resolved explicitly at scope time. Resolved silently mid-build, each of these becomes a defect nobody can attribute later.

by.description: Who decided. An unattributed decision is an assumption.

sourceDefects.description: Contradictions in the DESIGN source itself — a frame carrying another page's copy, one outlier font family, the same token in two colours, inconsistent gutters. Not build defects; reporting them as such wastes the reviewer's time. They belong to whoever owns the file.

resolution.description: What was built instead, and why.

handoffs.description: Steps the producer cannot perform, listed ONCE up front rather than discovered one interruption at a time.
